facts.text: The little grassbird is olive-brown to brown-grey, about 13 to 15 cm long, with a pale eyebrow and dark grey streaks on the throat, crown and cheeks.
facts.quote: It is an olive-brown/ brown-grey bird, measuring 13 to 15 cm, with a pale eyebrow and dark grey streaks in the throat, crown and cheeks.

facts.text: Its song is a plaintive, three-note monotone, often written as tee-ti-teee.
facts.quote: the voice is a "plaintive  three noted monotone, tee-ti-teee."

facts.text: In the breeding season it repeats a sequence of two to three plaintive piping whistles incessantly, so it is more often heard than seen.
facts.quote: particularly in the breeding season where it gives "a sequence of 2-3 plaintive piping whistles p-pee-pee repeated incessantly."

facts.text: The little grassbird eats insects and other small arthropods, staying hidden in the dense cover of grasses and swamp vegetation.
facts.quote: The little Grassbird eats insects and other small arthropods, usually remaining in the dense cover of grasses and swamp vegetation.

facts.text: It breeds from August to December or after rain, building a deep cup-shaped nest of grass, twigs and stems lined with feathers in tall grasses, reeds and low shrubs.
facts.quote: Nests are deep and cup-shaped consisting of grass, twigs and stems lined with feathers, typically of the Australasian swamphen (Porphyrio melanotus), and situated in tall grasses, reeds and low shrubs.

facts.text: A clutch contains 3-5 whitish or pink-white eggs speckled with grey.
facts.quote: A clutch consists of 3-5 whitish/pink-white, grey speckled eggs.

facts.text: The little grassbird lives in dense wetland vegetation, sedges, reeds and rank grass, and also uses lignum shrubs, saltmarsh and low mangroves.
facts.quote: It lives in dense wetland vegetation, sedges, reeds  and rank grass.  It also uses shrubs such as lignum, saltmarsh and low mangroves.

facts.text: After rain the little grassbird moves into temporary wetlands.
facts.quote: After rains the little grassbird will move into temporary wetlands.

facts.text: Male and female little grassbirds look indistinguishable to the naked eye, though males are larger in most measurements.
facts.quote: Adult male and female grassbirds are indistinguishable to the naked eye; however, males are larger for all parameters aside from the bill.

facts.text: The little grassbird is listed as Least Concern and its population trend appears to be increasing.
facts.quote: The species has been assessed as Least Concern by the IUCN. The population trend appears to be increasing
